newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle lightly trade at $65 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle lightly trade at $65 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle traded lightly at a steady $65.00 per cwt Wednesday, with a few feedlots passing $65.00 bids and still asking $66.00, feedlot sources said.

Cold weather spreading into the southern and central Plains had some cattle feeders requesting this week's sales be shipped quickly to prevent cattle weight loss and stress. In Kansas some cattle sold Tuesday were scheduled for shipment Thursday.
Feedlot managers said the cold already appeared to be slowing weight gains.
"It has hurt performance," said a Kansas feedlot manager.
Afternoon temperatures Wednesday were about 20 degrees Fahrenheit from western Kansas to the Texas Panhandle, sources in those areas said.
Low temperatures should drop to below zero in Kansas early Thursday and near zero in the Panhandle, meteorologists said.
USDA quoted midday beef prices up $0.25 per cwt to down $0.39 on 244 fabricated loads sold.
